{{Current events|year=2019|month=05|day=21|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflict and attacks
*Eleven people were killed in an ambush at 12th mile in Khonsa-Deomali road in Tirap District in Arunachal Pradesh. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-violence-arunachal/politician-family-members-among-11-killed-in-india-ambush-idUSKCN1SR188 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*Pharmaceutical giant [[Merck & Co.]] announces that it will purchase Peloton Therapeutics Inc. for $1.05 billion in cash. The catalyst for the deal is Peloton's recent progress in the development of a kidney cancer treatment. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-merck-co-deals/merck-buys-peloton-to-expand-its-kidney-cancer-treatment-portfolio-idUSKCN1SR136 (Reuters)]
*The [[Jamie Oliver#Jamie Oliver Restaurant Group|Jamie Oliver Restaurant Group]], owned by [[Britons|British]] [[restaurateur]] [[Jamie Oliver]], collapses into administration, resulting in 1,000 job losses. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-48352026 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]], [[Italy–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Venezuela]]'s Ambassador to [[Italy]], [[Isaías Rodríguez]], resigns, citing the government's lack of finances amid [[International sanctions during the Venezuelan crisis|international sanctions]] on the [[Nicolás Maduro]] government. Rodríguez says, due to the sanctions, he has been unable to pay his staff or the rent for his office in [[Rome]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/21/venezuelas-ambassador-to-italy-resigns (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*Aftermath of the [[Christchurch mosque shootings]]
**Brenton Tarrant, accused of killing 51 people and wounding 49 others in [[Christchurch mosque shootings|two New Zealand mosques]], is also charged with committing terrorist acts. [https://nypost.com/2019/05/21/alleged-christchurch-shooter-brenton-tarrant-charged-with-terrorism/ (''New York Post'')] [https://www.mid-day.com/articles/police-christchurch-attacker-brenton-tarrant-charged-with-terrorism/20989185 (''Mid Day'')]
*[[Washington (state)|Washington]] becomes the first [[United States|U.S.]] state to legalize [[human composting]], the right to allow people to have their body turned into [[soil]] after death. The process is seen as an alternative to traditional [[cremation]]s and [[burial]]s. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-48359571 (BBC News)]
*The [[California High-Speed Rail Authority]] sues the [[United States Department of Transportation|U.S. Transportation Department]] to block the cancelling of {{nowrap|$929 million}} [[Federal government of the United States|federal]] grant for the [[California High-Speed Rail]] project. The suit comes after the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] canceled the federal grant for [[California|California's]] bullet train on May 16, 2019. [https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-pol-ca-california-high-speed-rail-lawsuit-trump-administration-20190521-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')]
*[[2015–19 Irish gangland feud]]
**A man is shot dead and his car set alight in Walshestown near [[Balbriggan]], [[Dublin]]. It is believed the shooting is linked to the 2015–19 Irish gangland feud. [https://www.rte.ie/news (RTÉ)]
*Aftermath of the [[Mueller special counsel investigation]]
**The [[United States House Committee on the Judiciary]] subpoenas former [[White House Communications Director]] [[Hope Hicks]]  and former [[White House Counsel|Deputy White House Counsel]] [[Annie Donaldson]] in regards to their actions during the special counsel investigation into [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/house-panel-subpoenas-trumps-former-top-staffer-aide-to-mcgahn/2019/05/21/58182038-7801-11e9-ac17-284a66782c41_story.html?utm_term=.d5593a10e4cf (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Indonesian general election]]
**Indonesia's [[General Elections Commission]] announces that incumbent President [[Joko Widodo]] has won last month's presidential election, with 55.5% of the vote. His rival [[Prabowo Subianto]]'s team, however, refuses to sign and validate the results. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/21/indonesia-election-official-count-hands-victory-to-joko-widodo-as-rival-cries-foul (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Malawian general election]]
**Voters head to the polls to elect the next [[President of Malawi]], [[National Assembly (Malawi)|Parliament]] and local government councillors. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-48337392 (BBC News)] [https://www.france24.com/en/20190521-malawi-voters-polls-presidential-election-mutharika-chilima-chakwera (France 24)]
*[[2019 Pennsylvania's 12th congressional district special election]]
**Voters head to the polls in a special election to elect a new [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House Representative]] to finish the term for [[Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania's]] [[Pennsylvania's 12th congressional district|12th congressional district]] after Republican [[Tom Marino]] resigned on January 23, 2019. [http://www.fox29.com/news/local-news/what-you-need-to-know-about-the-pa-primary-special-elections (Fox Philadelphia)]
**[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Fred Keller (politician)|Fred Keller]] wins the special election against his [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] opponent Marc Friedenberg. [https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/444876-republican-wins-special-house-election-in-pennsylvania (''The Hill'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2019/05/21/us/elections/results-pennsylvania-elections.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The [[Catalonia|Catalan]] leaders who are imprisoned accused of rebellion, [[Oriol Junqueras]], [[Jordi Turull]], [[Jordi Sànchez]] and [[Josep Rull]], are sworn in as members of the [[Congress of Deputies]] after being elected in the [[April 2019 Spanish general election|28th April general election]] by an authorization of the [[Supreme Court of Spain|Supreme Court]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/jailed-deputies-allowed-to-attend-spanish-parliament-session (Fox News)]
**Catalan leader [[Raül Romeva]] is sworn in as [[Senate of Spain|Senator]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/congress/jailed-deputies-allowed-to-attend-spanish-parliament-session/2019/05/21/25705e28-7ba0-11e9-b1f3-b233fe5811ef_story.html?utm_term=.9903185136ea (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2019 Kentucky elections]]
**Incumbent [[Governor of Kentucky|Governor]] [[Matt Bevin]] wins the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nomination and [[Andy Beshear]] wins the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nomination primaries ahead of the November 5 [[2019 Kentucky gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/21/us/politics/kentucky-primary-elections.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.kentucky.com/news/politics-government/election/article230615424.html (''Lexington Herald-Leader'')] 
*[[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Ministry of Justice and Security|Minister of Justice and Security]] [[Mark Harbers]] resigns amid a scandal over a government report which played down crimes committed by [[asylum seeker]]s in the country, including rapes and murders, which were placed under a category called "other". The omission was first highlighted by Dutch newspaper ''[[De Telegraaf]]''. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190521-dutch-migration-minister-resigns-over-asylum-seeker-crime-report (FRANCE 24)]

;Sports
*[[2019 NBA playoffs]]
**The [[Golden State Warriors]] qualify for the [[NBA Finals]] for the fifth year in a row by defeating the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], 119–117, in [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] in Game 4 of the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/warriors/2019/05/20/golden-state-warriors-reach-nba-finals/3748577002/ (''USA Today'')]
